seo.title: How to Track AI Visibility: A Practical System
seo.meta_description: How to track AI visibility: answer checks, AI referral traffic, Search Console signals, branded search and leads, combined into a simple monthly report.

h1: How to Track AI Visibility: Mentions, Traffic and Leads in One Report
answer: To track AI visibility, combine four measures: regular checks of a fixed set of buyer questions in each AI assistant, AI referral traffic in Google Analytics, Search Console impressions and branded search trends, and leads by source. No single tool covers everything, so a simple monthly report that brings these together gives the clearest picture.
key_takeaways: No single tool measures all AI visibility.
Answer checks show whether and how you are mentioned.
Analytics shows visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity and others.
Search Console and branded search show indirect effects.
Leads by source connect visibility to revenue.

sections.heading: Why AI visibility is hard to track
sections.body_html: Traditional SEO tracking is mature: rankings, clicks and impressions for each keyword. AI visibility is messier. Answers vary each time they are generated, they differ between platforms, many do not produce a click, and Google counts its AI features within normal Search Console totals rather than separately. You need several measures that each show part of the picture.

sections.heading: Measure 1: answer checks
sections.body_html: Pick twenty to fifty real buyer questions and ask them in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, Claude and Google's AI features each month. Record whether you are mentioned, where in the answer, how you are described, which sources are cited and which competitors appear. This is the most direct measure of visibility and the only one that shows how AI describes you.

sections.heading: Measure 2: AI referral traffic
sections.body_html: In Google Analytics, look at sessions by source for AI platforms: chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, gemini.google.com, claude.ai, copilot.microsoft.com and others. Create a channel group or segment for them so they are easy to report. Track sessions, engagement and conversions. Some AI traffic arrives without referral information and appears as direct, so treat this number as a minimum.

sections.heading: Measure 3: Search Console
sections.body_html: Google includes clicks and impressions from AI Overviews and AI Mode in its standard web search reports. Watch impressions for question-style queries and for the pages you optimized. Rising impressions with flat clicks may mean your pages are being shown or used in AI answers without a click.

sections.heading: Measure 4: branded demand
sections.body_html: When AI answers mention you, some people search for your brand afterwards. Track branded search impressions in Search Console and direct traffic over time. A steady rise in branded demand alongside better answer checks is a strong sign that AI visibility is working, even if referral traffic is small.

sections.heading: Measure 5: leads by source
sections.body_html: Record the source of every lead: form, call or booking. Add a "how did you hear about us?" field with options such as ChatGPT or another AI assistant. Many buyers will tell you directly. Connecting visibility to leads is what turns AI tracking from a curiosity into a business case.

sections.heading: A one-page monthly report
sections.body_html:
SectionWhat to show
Answer checksShare of voice, mentions by platform, notable changes
AI referralsSessions and conversions by AI platform
Search ConsoleImpressions and clicks for question queries and key pages
Branded demandBranded impressions and direct traffic trend
LeadsLeads by source, including self-reported AI
ActionsWhat changed and what to do next

sections.heading: Pages and indexing
sections.body_html: Before anything else, confirm that the pages you want cited are indexed. In Search Console, check that new pages appear in the index and begin to show impressions. For Bing, which powers Copilot and some other tools, use Bing Webmaster Tools. A page that is not indexed cannot be cited by AI tools that rely on these indexes.

sections.heading: Common tracking mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Checking AI answers once and treating the result as permanent.
  • Changing the question set every month, so trends mean nothing.
  • Ignoring direct and branded traffic.
  • Reporting mentions without checking accuracy.
  • Not connecting any of it to leads.

sections.heading: Tools that help
sections.body_html: Google Search Console and Google Analytics are free and essential. Bing Webmaster Tools covers Bing. Dedicated AI visibility tools automate answer checks across platforms. A spreadsheet works for answer checks at small scale. The tool matters less than doing the same measurements consistently every month.

sections.heading: Setting up an AI channel in Google Analytics
sections.body_html: In Google Analytics, you can create a custom channel group that collects sessions from AI platforms into one channel. Define it with a rule matching session sources such as chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, gemini.google.com, claude.ai and copilot.microsoft.com, and place it above the referral channel so these sessions are not counted as ordinary referrals. Once set up, reports and dashboards show AI traffic as its own line, with engagement and conversions, which makes monthly reporting much faster.

sections.heading: An example monthly summary
sections.body_html: "This month we were mentioned in 9 of 30 tracked answers, up from 6. ChatGPT now names us for two comparison questions where it previously named only competitors. AI referral sessions rose from 41 to 58, with four form leads, and branded search impressions grew 12%. One assistant still lists our old office address; we have corrected two directories that showed it. Next month we will publish the pricing guide and recheck." A summary like this tells a team what happened, why it matters and what comes next.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Track whether AI tools mention you, whether people visit from them, whether your brand demand grows and whether leads follow. Use the same questions and methods every month and connect the results to revenue.

faqs.q: How do I track AI visibility?
faqs.a: Combine monthly answer checks in each assistant, AI referral traffic in Google Analytics, Search Console impressions, branded search trends and leads by source.

faqs.q: Can Google Search Console show AI Overview traffic?
faqs.a: Google includes clicks and impressions from AI features in standard web search reports, but does not break them out separately.

faqs.q: How do I see ChatGPT traffic in Google Analytics?
faqs.a: Look at sessions by source for chatgpt.com, and create a channel group for AI platforms so they are easy to report.

faqs.q: Why is some AI traffic shown as direct?
faqs.a: Some apps and links do not pass referral information, so visits arrive as direct traffic. Treat AI referral numbers as a minimum.

faqs.q: How often should I track AI visibility?
faqs.a: Monthly is a good rhythm, using the same questions and methods each time.

faqs.q: What is the best AI visibility tool?
faqs.a: There is no single best tool. Free Google and Bing tools plus consistent answer checks cover the essentials; paid tools automate at scale.

faqs.q: How do I know AI visibility leads to sales?
faqs.a: Track leads by source, including a "how did you hear about us" field with AI assistants as an option.

faqs.q: Should I track every AI platform?
faqs.a: Track the ones your buyers use most. For most businesses that includes ChatGPT, Google's AI features, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot.

faqs.q: What is a good AI referral number?
faqs.a: There is no universal benchmark. Compare your own numbers month to month, and look at engagement and conversions, not just sessions.
